**Selecting 4+4 predecode**

</think>

{
  "candidate_rtl": "module decoder_8bit
#(
    parameter N = 8
) (
    input [N-1:0] in,
    output reg [(1<<N)-1:0] out
);
    generate
        if (N == 8) begin : g_decode8
            wire [15:0] low_n;
            wire [15:0] high_n;

            for (genvar p = 0; p < 16; p = p + 1) begin : g_predecode
                assign low_n[p]  = ~(in[3:0] == p);
                assign high_n[p] = ~(in[7:4] == p);
            end

            for (genvar q = 0; q < 256; q = q + 1) begin : g_output
                always @(*) begin
                    out[q] = ~(low_n[q % 16] | high_n[q / 16]);
                end
            end
        end else begin : g_other_width
            always @(*) begin
                out = {{(1<<N)-1{1'b0}}, 1'b1} << in;
            end
        end
    endgenerate
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The variable shift can synthesize into a deep selection network. The decoder also has substantial input and shared-term fanout across its 256 outputs.",
  "rewrite": "Replace the fixed eight-bit instance with two shared active-low 4-to-16 predecoders and 256 two-input NOR combinations. Each output selects exactly one low-nibble term and one high-nibble term.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to reduce maximum data arrival by exposing a shallow predecode-and-combine implementation rather than a variable-shift network. Actual timing improvement requires mapping and STA; no measured gain is claimed.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Uses 32 shared predecode terms and 256 final combinations before technology mapping and fanout buffering. Area, maximum slew, and maximum capacitance must be verified against the specified limits.",
  "functional_boundaries": "For N=8, output bit q is asserted exactly when in equals q, for every binary input. The module name, ports, widths, unsigned declarations, parameter declaration and default are preserved. Other parameter values retain the original expression. The design is entirely combinational with fully defined outputs and no storage."
}
